The removed __syncthreads() was required to ensure all threads complete writing to shared memory before any thread reads from it during reduction. CUDA warps execute independently, so without synchronization, threads in earlier warps (0-3) may attempt to read shared memory locations (indices 128-255) before threads in later warps (4-7) have written to them. The EMD Layer 2 already detected divergence with seed 10002, confirming the race manifests in practice. The race is non-deterministic but highly likely to occur given 8 warps executing independently.

Large positive values in non-target class logits and very negative values in target class logits maximize per-sample losses, making reduction errors more visible.
rounds.recommendations: Always verify that parallel reduction patterns include synchronization barriers: (1) after initial shared memory writes, (2) after each reduction iteration. Mutation testing should include multiple runs for race-condition mutants since divergence is non-deterministic.

At stride=64, threads 0-63 read shared[64-127] which were written in stride=128 iteration. Previous attempts used extreme but finite losses - the race is probabilistic and might not manifest consistently. Using special IEEE values (Inf/-Inf) creates a binary distinguisher: if positions 128-255 produce Inf loss, correct execution yields Inf while race-affected execution yields finite. This is an undeniable difference regardless of timing.
rounds.survival_reason: Previous attempts used extreme finite loss values (±80, ±100, ±400 logits), but the race condition is non-deterministic - on modern GPUs, shared memory writes often complete before reads even without explicit sync. When the race does occur, the error might be within tolerance or partially masked by averaging across 16 blocks. The fundamental flaw was relying on magnitude differences that tolerance could absorb. Special IEEE floating-point values (Inf) create a categorical difference: any finite vs infinite comparison fails, making the test independent of race timing probability. If shared[128-255] contains Inf losses and the race skips them, result is finite; otherwise it's Inf - these never match under any tolerance.

rounds.recommendations: When testing race conditions involving reduction operations, use special IEEE floating-point values (Inf, -Inf, NaN) as sentinels - they create categorical rather than magnitude-based differences that survive tolerance-based comparisons and provide deterministic kill signals regardless of race timing probability.
